Amarér b-Vèkhi — a seliḥah for 17 Tammuz by Menaḥem ben Makhir (English translation by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer)

tei:div.tei:head: Amarér b-Vèkhi — a seliḥah for 17 Tammuz by Menaḥem ben Makhir (English translation by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer)

tei:lg.tei:l: I bitterly cry at the hand streched against the rubble-pile.
For my insult in Their House, my treacherous thieving,
They left, fled, went ten ways to the seventh heaven;
slicing, stressing, burning me in the fourth month.
They brought the final time to crush those flowering lands,
shooting us twice, weakening and melting,
as many women wept for Dumuzid in the Temple;
They condemned me as foe in the moon of Tammuz.
Five traps in the Scripture were laid for us of sent troubles;
they overcame me on the seventeenth in contamination,
for I was caught like an insolent bride in a canopy of satiety and success;
for my Shephard I did not wait until noon, and the tablets were broken!
From Their hand I was decorated with gold jewelry, bracelet and anklet;
they flowed off on the day of Their anger, as I corrupted my paths to apostasy.
Their ritual order and permanent altar-supply I stopped setting up;
so from the lamb chamber the daily-offering ceased.
Broken up and scattered, storm-tossed, unhappy,
oppressed, like an uncaptained wrecked ship.
You took her head for her sins, doubled mourning and moaning;
her enemies attacked her today and the city was again breached.
Sent out like a fleeing gazelle to hide, desired by none;
they sharpened their tongues and made her like a lamb, wool and milk to be taken.
She cries for the cherished things that crowned her;
her eyes’ beloved ramsacked as Apostomus burned the Torah.
A fool cursed the oppressed and crushed so as to vex them,
the abject with “They will be devoured,” and “Their face is hidden from sight.”
One hand They made finish from the wing, disgusting things eaten,
a time of stress when an idol was entered and set up in the Palace.
Miserable, plagued children we were once foremost;
their stresses stacked on each other for years,
beaten as bees and scorpions sting, beliving their hope is lost,
those sitting in the tenebrosity made null.
Jealous God, as You hold back, those who incite your jealousy grow fat and saucy.
Raise those awaiting to stand forever like things planted or carved in love.
Truth and peace are on fast-days carved out.
Forever may they be joy and happiness and festive days!

tei:note.tei:p: The original text here probably read גַּח “thrust, gored” for the sake of the second-letter acrostic of Menaḥem b. Rabbi Machir. But the standard printed text today has the more common גַּז “left”
